definition: THEREFROM, adverb. From this or that.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: US-WARD, adverb. Toward us; in our direction or with reference to us.
YOU-WARD, adverb. Toward you; in your direction or with reference to you.
THEE-WARD, adverb. Toward thee; in thy direction or with reference to thee.
ALLOWETH, third-person singular form of ALLOW. Permits, admits, approves, or acknowledges. See ALLOW.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: APPROVEST, second-person singular form of APPROVE. Thou dost approve: to like, admit as right, commend, prove, or show to be worthy. See APPROVE.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: CHIMNEY, noun. A passage or flue through which smoke and heated air ascend from a fire.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: CONDITION, noun. State or particular mode of being; quality; circumstance; rank; or the terms and stipulations of an agreement.
source_title: American Dictionary of the English Language

definition: COSTLINESS, noun. Expensiveness; great cost or value; the quality of being costly.
DELICACIES, plural of DELICACY. Choice or pleasing foods, luxuries, or refined enjoyments.
EXCLUDED, participle passive. Shut out; debarred; excepted; prevented from entering or sharing.
EXCUSING, participle present. Freeing or seeking to free from blame; offering a reason in defense; serving as an excuse.
HERDMAN, noun. One who tends or keeps a herd; a herdsman.
INSTRUCTORS, plural of INSTRUCTOR. Teachers; those who communicate knowledge, direction, or discipline.
LINEAGE, noun. Descent in a line from a common ancestor; race; family line; progeny.
MISCARRYING, participle present. Failing to carry safely or successfully; in Hosea 9:14, failing to bring a child to a living birth.
RARE, adjective. Uncommon; scarce; seldom found. In Daniel 2:11, exceptionally difficult or beyond ordinary ability.
A man at Lydda who had kept his bed eight years with palsy and was healed when Peter said, 'Jesus Christ maketh thee whole.'
An encampment of Israel in the wilderness journey, named after Dibon-gad and before the mountains of Abarim.
A name or title connected with a king to whom Israel looked for help in Hosea. The passages show that this foreign help could not heal or deliver them.
A town named within the inheritance of the tribe of Dan.
A town named within the inheritance of the tribe of Benjamin.
A town named within the inheritance of the tribe of Issachar.
A town associated with the settlements of Simeon.
A boundary location named in the description of the inheritance of Zebulun.
ASSYRIAN, noun or adjective. An inhabitant or representative of Assyria; of or belonging to Assyria. See ASSYRIA.
source_file: KJV: Hosea 5:13; 11:5; 12:1; Easton's Bible Dictionary: Assyria

definition: FIRSTRIPE, noun. The first-ripe or earliest fruit; in Hosea 9:10, the first ripe fruit of the fig tree. See Strong's H1063.
TYRUS, noun. The KJV form of Tyre, the ancient Phoenician city. See TYRE.
source_file: KJV: Hosea 9:13; Easton's Bible Dictionary: Tyre

definition: INASMUCH, conjunction or adverb. Seeing that; since; because; or to the extent that.
HOUSETOP, noun. The roof or upper surface of a house.
HUNDREDFOLD, adverb or noun. A hundred times as much; in a hundredfold measure.
The surname or designation of Judas, one of the twelve, who betrayed Jesus.
A city east of Jordan associated with Gilead and Gad and assigned to the Levites.
A name borne by Nahor's wife, the daughter of Haran, and by a daughter of Zelophehad.
A name borne by several Israelites, including the mother named in Leviticus 24:11 and persons named in the genealogies and service records of Chronicles.
A name used for more than one biblical place, including locations connected with Canaan's boundaries and battles with the Philistines.
A name borne by several men, including the father of Bezaleel and the father of Geber.
A name used for a Manassite family associated with Gideon and for an Anethothite numbered among David's mighty men.
A KJV place name used for locations connected with Dan, Zebulun, and the Levitical cities. The alternate spelling Ajalon also appears in the KJV.
The land in which Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh were named, and to which the vessels of the house of God were carried in Daniel's day.
A name borne by several Israelites, including a chief of the sons of Merari and a servant of King Josiah.
A name borne by several men, including a son of Neariah and the governor of the house who was slain by Zichri.
A name borne by several Israelites, including the head of a priestly course and a man who helped repair Jerusalem's wall.
The name of an Israelite wilderness encampment and of men named in the genealogies of Levi and Ephraim.
source_title: KJV Bible Name and Place Guide

definition: The father named with Jehoshaphat the recorder and with Baana, one of Solomon's officers.
A name borne by several men, including a Korhite who came to David, a musician, and a prince of the tribe of Dan.
EPHRAIMITE, noun or adjective. A member or descendant of Ephraim; belonging to the tribe of Ephraim.
The KJV New Testament form of Gomorrah, the city named with Sodom as an example of divine judgment. See GOMORRAH.
A designation applied to Shammah, Ahiam, and other men named in the records of David's mighty men.
A designation applied to Mebunnai and Sibbecai or Sibbechai in records of David's mighty men and military captains.
A woman of Jezreel; the designation used of Ahinoam, David's wife and the mother of Amnon.
The father of Jeshua, the priest who helped build the altar and the house of God after the captivity.
The KJV New Testament form of Noah, who entered the ark before the flood. See NOAH.
A family name among those who returned from the captivity and were recorded in Ezra and Nehemiah.
PERIZZITE, noun or adjective. One of the Perizzites, a people dwelling in Canaan and repeatedly listed among the peoples of the land.
A son of Peleg and the father of Serug in the genealogy from Shem toward Abraham.
The son of Zurishaddai, prince and captain of the children of Simeon during Israel's wilderness journey.
A descendant of Judah who had daughters but no sons and gave one daughter in marriage to his Egyptian servant Jarha.
SIDONIANS, plural noun. The people of Sidon, noted in the KJV among the inhabitants of the land and for skill in cutting timber.
A city in Egypt where a group from Judah came and where the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
UPSIDE, noun used in the phrase upside down. Inverted, overturned, or thrown into disorder.
A name borne by several Israelites, including Samuel's son and Hezron's wife.
A name borne by a son of Ulla and associated with a family recorded among those who returned from captivity.
A city of the Jews and the home of Joseph, the disciple who requested and took the body of Jesus for burial.
A city named in the inheritances of Judah and Simeon and later listed with its suburbs among the Levitical cities.
A name borne by several men in Chronicles, including a descendant of Sheshan and a man numbered among those who came to David.
A family name among those who returned from captivity and a name listed among the covenant signers in Nehemiah.
BEEROTHITE, noun or adjective. A person of Beeroth; the plural denotes its inhabitants. The designation is applied to Rimmon and Naharai in Second Samuel.
DANITES, plural noun. Members or descendants of the tribe of Dan.
A name associated with two family groups recorded among the temple servants and the servants of Solomon who returned from captivity.
GILEADITES, plural noun. Members of the family descended from Gilead or inhabitants and men of Gilead.
A man of the land of Temani who reigned as a king of Edom after Jobab.
A name used in genealogical records for a son or descendant of Dan, for sons of Aher, and for a wife of Shaharaim.
A place name connected with the Emims at Shaveh Kiriathaim and later listed among the cities of Moab.
A town built with Ono and later named among the places whose families returned from captivity and resettled the land.
MAACHATHITE, noun or adjective. A person of the Maachathites; the plural names a people whose border is associated with Geshur and Bashan.
A son of Uzziel and the father of Shamir in the Levitical genealogies of Chronicles.
The name appearing with Pilate, the governor of Judaea before whom Christ Jesus witnessed a good confession.
A man of Masrekah who reigned as a king of Edom after Hadad.
The KJV New Testament form of Sarah, Abraham's wife and the mother who received strength to conceive the promised son. See SARAH.
SARDIUS, noun. A precious stone named in the high priest's breastplate, among the stones of Ezekiel 28, and among the foundations of New Jerusalem.
SHOULDERPIECES, plural noun. The parts of the ephod joined at its upper edges and used in fastening its chains and settings.
A son or descendant of Ephraim and the family head from whom the Shuthalhites were named.
A Christian minister named with Paul and Timotheus in the epistle greetings and called a faithful brother by Peter.
A name borne by men in the genealogies of Manasseh and Benjamin; the sons of the Benjamite Ulam were mighty archers.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Amminadab, an ancestor named in the genealogy of Jesus Christ. See AMMINADAB.
A son of Benjamin and the family head from whom the Ashbelites were named.
A KJV spelling of Ashkelon, a city of the Philistines. See ASHKELON.
A boundary point named in the description of the southern border of Israel and Judah.
A name borne by several men, including a head of a Manassite family and the fathers of Jerimoth and Seraiah.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Boaz, the son of Salmon and Rachab, husband of Ruth, and father of Obed. See BOAZ.
A KJV spelling of Elath, a place beside Ezion-geber on the shore of the Red sea in the land of Edom. See ELATH.
GALILAEAN, noun or adjective. A person of Galilee; belonging to Galilee.
GERSHONITE, noun or adjective. A member or descendant of the family of Gershon; belonging to that family.
The KJV name for Greece in Daniel's references to its king, prince, and realm. See GREECE.
HAGARITES, plural noun. A people east of Gilead against whom the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half Manasseh made war.
A place name used for a city of Judah assigned to the Levites and for a place in Moab named in Jeremiah's judgment prophecy.
A name borne by Levites, including the first of Rehabiah's sons and the brother of Michah.
IZHARITES, plural noun. Descendants of Izhar among the Levites; men of this family served as officers and judges.
A city in the inheritance of Reuben, assigned with its suburbs to the Levites, and later named in judgment upon Moab.
The designation applied to Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who wholly followed the LORD God of Israel.
LEANFLESHED, adjective. Having little flesh; very thin or gaunt. Used of the ill-favoured kine in Pharaoh's dream.
A personal and place name used of Talmai's daughter, the mother of Absalom, and of a Syrian kingdom or people allied with Ammon.
source_title: KJV Bible Name and Place Guide

definition: The KJV New Testament spelling of Manasseh, used of the king in Christ's genealogy and of the tribe in Revelation. See MANASSEH.
MANASSITES, plural noun. Members or descendants of the tribe of Manasseh.
A name borne by several Israelites recorded in Ezra and by a priestly representative named in Nehemiah.
MIDIANITISH, adjective. Of or belonging to Midian; used of Cozbi, the daughter of Zur.
The false god and abomination of the children of Ammon after whom Solomon went and for whom he built a high place.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Nahshon, the son of Aminadab and an ancestor named in the genealogy of Jesus Christ. See NAHSHON.
A name borne by a man in the royal genealogy of Judah and by a Simeonite captain who went to mount Seir.
The firstborn son of Ishmael and the brother named in connection with the marriages of Mahalath and Bashemath.
OBSCURITY, noun. Darkness, dimness, or a state lacking light; used in Isaiah in contrast with light and brightness.
A KJV place name for the land associated with the Philistines in Exodus and Isaiah. See PHILISTIA.
A name borne by a son of Shobal and associated with a family of temple servants who returned from captivity.
A name appearing in Levitical service lists among the sons of Amram and in a division of twelve with his sons and brethren.
SIMEONITES, plural noun. Members or descendants of the tribe of Simeon.
SNUFFDISHES, plural noun. Vessels belonging to the service of the candlestick, listed with its lamps, tongs, and snuffers and made of pure gold.
TEKOITE, noun. A person of Tekoa; the designation applied to Ira the son of Ikkesh, one of David's mighty men and a captain over a monthly course.
WOMENSERVANTS, plural noun. Female servants; women serving in a household.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Ahaz, the son of Jotham and father of Hezekiah in the genealogy of Jesus Christ. See AHAZ.
A name borne by an Israelite listed among the sons of Pahath-moab and by a priestly representative named in Nehemiah.
The name of an officer over the tribute in David's administration and of the man sent by Rehoboam whom Israel stoned.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Hagar, used in Paul's allegory of the two covenants and associated there with mount Sinai and bondage. See HAGAR.
AMRAMITES, plural noun. The family descended from Amram among the Kohathites and Levites.
A personal name appearing in Levitical and priestly genealogies in Chronicles and Nehemiah.
A name appearing among the men who stood beside Ezra as he read the law and among those recorded with the covenant names.
A son of Nadab and father of Ishi in the genealogy of Judah.
The KJV spelling of Arpad, a city or kingdom named by the Assyrian spokesman among places unable to resist Assyria. See ARPAD.
ARVADITE, noun. A member of one of the families of Canaan, named with the Zemarite and the Hamathite.
A servant of king Josiah sent with Hilkiah and others to inquire of Huldah the prophetess after the book of the law was found.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Asher, used of the tribe to which Anna belonged and of the sealed tribe in Revelation. See ASHER.
The KJV spelling of Ashkenaz, a son of Gomer and the name of a kingdom summoned against Babylon. See ASHKENAZ.
A son of Hezron and Abiah who is called the father of Tekoa.
A descendant of Manasseh from whom came the family of the Asrielites.
A KJV name for Assyria or its people, used of Esar-haddon king of Assur and of the power allied with the children of Lot. See ASSYRIA.
AUL, noun. A pointed tool used for piercing; in the law, used to bore the ear of a servant who chose lasting service. A spelling of awl.
A people named near the Philistine territory in Joshua and also the people who made Nibhaz and Tartak after being settled in Samaria.
The city of Hadad the son of Bedad, an Edomite king who smote Midian in the field of Moab.
AXLETREES, plural noun. The shafts or supporting centers upon which wheels turn; named among the molten parts of the temple bases.
The son of Meshullam and father of Shaphan the scribe, who served during the reign of Josiah.
A city named among the southern towns of Judah and within the inheritance of Simeon.
A man in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, named as the son of Eliakim and father of Sadoc.
A name borne by the father of Hananiah the prophet of Gibeon and by the father of Jaazaniah, a prince seen by Ezekiel.
A city in the land of Shinar, at the beginning of Nimrod's kingdom, named in connection with the LORD's confounding of human language and scattering of the people.
The name associated with a family of temple servants who returned from captivity with Zerubbabel.
The father of Hadad, an Edomite king who smote Midian in the field of Moab.
The name associated with a family of temple servants listed among those who returned from captivity.
One of the six sons of Azel in the genealogy of Benjamin.
BROKENHEARTED, adjective. Crushed, deeply afflicted, or wounded in spirit; those whom the anointed Servant was sent to bind up and heal.
BUZITE, noun. The designation applied to Elihu the son of Barachel, of the kindred of Ram.
CANAANITISH, adjective. Of or belonging to the Canaanites; used of the mother of Shaul, a son of Simeon.
CARMELITESS, noun. A woman of Carmel; the designation applied to Abigail, formerly the wife of Nabal and later a wife of David.
CHALDEAN, noun or adjective. A person of Chaldea or belonging to the Chaldeans; used of Nebuchadnezzar and of a member of the learned court group in Babylon.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Canaan, the land named in Stephen's address and Paul's sermon at Antioch. See CANAAN.
CHESNUT, noun. A KJV tree name, used of rods selected by Jacob and of trees in the garden-of-God comparison in Ezekiel.
A KJV place name associated with the northern plains and the inland sea called the sea of Chinneroth. See CHINNERETH.
CLIFTS, plural noun. Clefts, recesses, or steep broken places in valleys and rocks.
CUCKOW, noun. A KJV bird name included among the birds Israel was forbidden to eat under the law.
CYRENIAN, noun or adjective. A person of Cyrene or belonging to Cyrene; used of Simon, who was compelled to bear the cross after Jesus.
A descendant of Joktan named in the genealogies of Genesis and Chronicles.
EKRONITES, plural noun. The inhabitants of Ekron, one of the five principal Philistine groups and cities.
A word spoken twice by Jesus from the cross and interpreted by Mark as My God.
The son of Zabad and father of Obed in the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles.
A son of Gad from whom came the family of the Erites.
EVENINGTIDE, noun. The time of evening; the latter part or close of the day.
A name borne by a son of Gad and by a son of Bela, a Benjamite head of a father's house.
FATFLESHED, adjective. Having abundant flesh; plump or well fed. Used of the seven well-favoured kine in Pharaoh's dream.
A name borne by a son of Ephah, Caleb's concubine, and by a son of Haran in the genealogy of Judah.
A KJV geographical and people name associated with the border country of Geshur and land that remained to be possessed.
source_title: KJV Bible Place and People Guide

definition: A son of Aram named in the genealogies of Genesis and Chronicles.
GIBEONITE, noun or adjective. A person of Gibeon or belonging to Gibeon; used of Ismaiah and Melatiah.
A son of Heman appointed with his sons and brethren to the twenty-second course of temple music service.
GIER, noun. Part of the KJV bird name gier eagle, included among the birds Israel was forbidden to eat under the law.
GILONITE, noun or adjective. A person of Giloh or belonging to Giloh; the designation applied to Ahithophel, David's counsellor.
GRAPEGATHERERS, plural noun. People who gather or harvest grapes; used in the prophets' comparison concerning gleanings left behind.
The name associated with a family of priests listed among those who returned from captivity.
A son of Gad from whom came the family of the Haggites.
A KJV spelling of Ai, the place east of Beth-el near which Abram pitched his tent, built an altar, and called upon the name of the LORD. See AI.
HAMATHITE, noun. A member of one of the families of Canaan, named with the Arvadite and Zemarite.
A KJV spelling of Enoch, used in Chronicles both of the patriarchal line before the flood and of a son of Midian. See ENOCH.
HEZRONITES, plural noun. A family name applied to descendants of men named Hezron in the tribes of Reuben and Judah.
The former inhabitants of Seir who were destroyed and displaced by the children of Esau.
A son of Heman appointed with his sons and brethren to the twenty-first course of temple music service.
A man named by Paul among those delivered unto Satan to learn not to blaspheme and among false teachers whose word would eat as a canker.
The father of Micaiah the prophet, whom the king of Israel disliked because he prophesied evil concerning him.
ISHMAELITES, plural noun. A people descended from or associated with Ishmael, named in Judges and among the nations joined against Israel in a psalm.
A son of Uzzi and father of Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Ishiah, all chief men in Issachar's genealogy.
A son of Onam, brother of Shammai, and father of Jether and Jonathan in the genealogy of Judah.
An Egyptian servant of Sheshan who married Sheshan's daughter and became the father of Attai.
A KJV place name for Jerusalem in the border description and city list of Benjamin. See JERUSALEM and JEBUS.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Jeconiah, named in the genealogy of Jesus Christ at the time of the carrying away to Babylon and as the father of Salathiel. See JECONIAH.
A chief father among the Gershonite sons of Laadan and father of Zetham and Joel, who were over the treasures of the house of the LORD.
The daughter of king Jehoram, sister of Ahaziah, and wife of Jehoiada the priest, who hid Joash from Athaliah and preserved his life. See JEHOSHEBA.
The name Moses gave Oshea the son of Nun, later commonly rendered Joshua, and used again in his genealogy. See JOSHUA.
A son of Simeon named in the family records of Genesis and Exodus.
JERAHMEELITES, plural noun. A clan or people associated with the south of Judah and with cities to which David sent spoil.
A name used of a man in the genealogy from Adam and of the father of Gedor in a genealogy of Judah; the first is elsewhere rendered Jared.
The KJV New Testament form of Jeremiah, the prophet named in Matthew's fulfillment statements. See JEREMIAH.
A name borne by men listed among the captains and people who came to Gedaliah and later approached Jeremiah after Jerusalem's fall.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Jotham, the son of Ozias and father of Achaz in the genealogy of Jesus Christ. See JOTHAM.
The name associated with a family of temple servants listed among those who returned from captivity.
A son or descendant of Javan named in the genealogies of Genesis and Chronicles. See CHITTIM.
LIBNITES, plural noun. A Levitical family descended through Gershon and named among the families of Levi.
LICENCE, noun. Permission, leave, or liberty granted to speak or act.
LUNATICK, noun or adjective. A historical KJV term for a person suffering a recurring severe affliction; Matthew records such sufferers among those Jesus healed.
A duke of Edom named among the chiefs descended from Esau.
MAHLITES, plural noun. A Levitical family belonging to the line of Merari.
MANAHETHITES, plural noun. A family or clan named in the genealogies of Judah in connection with Shobal and Salma.
The parent of Mehetabel and child of Mezahab, named in the record of an Edomite king's family.
The title identified and interpreted in John's Gospel as the Christ.
A name recorded in the sixth priestly course and among the covenant names in Nehemiah.
MORASTHITE, noun or adjective. A person of Moresheth or belonging to it; the designation applied to Micah the prophet.
MUSHITES, plural noun. A Levitical family belonging to the line of Merari and descended from Mushi.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Naphtali, used of the tribal territory named in Matthew's account of Jesus dwelling in Capernaum. See NAPHTALI.
source_title: KJV Bible Place and People Guide

definition: NETOPHATHITES, plural noun. A family or inhabitants associated with Netophah and its villages.
A place in Moab known for its waters, whose desolation is named in prophecies of judgment upon Moab.
The former name of Joshua the son of Nun before Moses called him Jehoshua. See JOSHUA and JEHOSHUA.
OVERPAST, adjective. Passed over, gone by, or ended.
A people descended from Mizraim and named in the genealogies of Genesis and Chronicles.
The servant who accompanied Gideon to the outside of the Midianite host before Gideon's attack.
A son of Micah named in the genealogy of Benjamin.
The name associated with Pochereth of Zebaim and a family recorded in the return lists of Ezra and Nehemiah.
PRACTISED, verb. Planned, carried on, or performed an action; used of mischief and of an evil power's activity.
PRANSINGS, plural noun. Vigorous, bounding, or dashing movements of horses.
PUBLICKLY, adverb. Openly, before the people, or in a public setting. A historical spelling of publicly.
The chief city of the children of Ammon, named in connection with Og's bedstead and a prophecy of the sword. See RABBAH.
RESPITE, noun. A temporary relief, pause, or delay from pressure or trouble.
RESTORER, noun. One who restores, renews, repairs, or brings back to a sound condition.
RESTRAIN, verb. To hold back, limit, check, or keep within bounds.
REVELLINGS, plural noun. Disorderly or excessive festivities associated in the New Testament with drunkenness, lust, and former sinful living.
The father of Ittai, or Ithai, a Benjamite from Gibeah named among David's mighty men.
RICHLY, adverb. Abundantly, plentifully, or in full measure.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Rehoboam, the son of Solomon and father of Abia in the genealogy of Jesus Christ. See REHOBOAM.
A city at the extent of Bashan in the former kingdom of Og and near the territory occupied by the children of Gad.
A boundary point in the inheritance of the tribe of Zebulun.
SCARCELY, adverb. Barely, hardly, or only with difficulty.
SECURELY, adverb. Safely, confidently, or without expectation of danger.
SERJEANTS, plural noun. Officers or official messengers serving the magistrates. A historical spelling of sergeants.
A town where Amorites continued to dwell and later a place within one of Solomon's administrative districts. See SHAALABBIN.
SHAALBONITE, noun or adjective. A person of Shaalbon or belonging to it; the designation applied to Eliahba, one of David's mighty men.
A KJV place element used in Shaveh Kiriathaim and in the valley of Shaveh, which is called the king's dale.
SHEEPCOTE, noun. An enclosure or shelter for sheep; the place from which the LORD took David to rule Israel.
SHERIFFS, plural noun. Officials named among the rulers of the Babylonian provinces summoned by Nebuchadnezzar.
The father of Azubah and maternal grandfather of king Jehoshaphat.
A son of Naphtali from whom came the family of the Shillemites.
The name associated with a family of porters listed among those who returned from captivity.
A town belonging to Judah where the Philistine armies gathered before the conflict in which David faced Goliath. See SHOCHO and SOCHO.
SHUHAMITES, plural noun. The family descended from Shuham in the tribe of Dan.
A Hushathite warrior who slew Saph, also called Sippai, one of the descendants of the giant during war with the Philistines.
SIGNIFIED, verb. Made known, indicated, declared, or communicated.
SIXSCORE, adjective or noun. Six times twenty; one hundred and twenty.
SOBERLY, adverb. With sound judgment, self-control, moderation, and seriousness.
SORELY, adverb. Greatly, severely, or grievously.
SPEAKER, noun. One who speaks; a spokesman or person prominent in addressing others.
SPEARMEN, plural noun. Men armed with spears; soldiers equipped for fighting or guard duty.
SPECIAL, adjective. Particular, distinguished, chosen, or beyond what is ordinary.
STEDFASTNESS, noun. Firmness, stability, constancy, or settled faithfulness.
STOUTHEARTED, adjective. Bold, unyielding, or obstinate in heart; used of mighty men and of those far from righteousness.
STUMBLINGSTONE, noun. A stone or obstacle over which one stumbles; used figuratively in Romans of Christ to those seeking righteousness by works rather than faith.
SUFFICIENTLY, adverb. Enough, adequately, or in a measure that meets the need.
SWADDLED, verb. Wrapped or bound in cloth as an infant; by extension, tenderly cared for in infancy.
THIRTYFOLD, adjective or adverb. Thirty times as much or in thirtyfold measure.
THRESHINGFLOORS, plural noun. Prepared places where grain was threshed and separated from chaff.
The king of Hamath who, after David defeated Hadarezer, sent his son Hadoram to greet and congratulate David with valuable vessels.
TRAVELLER, noun. A person making a journey; a wayfaring person or guest from the road.
UNBLAMEABLE, adjective. Free from blame or accusation; not open to just reproach.
UNMOVEABLE, adjective. Unable to be moved; fixed, firm, or steadfast.
UPHOLDEN, verb. Supported, sustained, strengthened, or kept from falling.
A name borne by a descendant of Pharez living at Jerusalem and by a man of the sons of Bigvai who returned with Ezra.
UZZIELITES, plural noun. A Levitical family descended from Uzziel among the Kohathites.
WARRIORS, plural noun. Soldiers, fighters, or men trained and chosen for war.
WASHPOT, noun. A vessel used for washing; used figuratively of Moab in the psalms.
WATCHER, noun. In Daniel's vision, a holy heavenly messenger who came down from heaven and announced the decree concerning the king.
WATCHERS, plural noun. Those who watch or observe; used of threatening watchers from a far country in Jeremiah and of holy heavenly agents in Daniel.
WATERSPRINGS, plural noun. Springs, fountains, or sources from which water flows.
WAYSIDE, noun. The side or edge of a road or traveled way.
WEAKENETH, verb. Makes weak; reduces strength, courage, power, or effectiveness.
WELLPLEASING, adjective. Acceptable, agreeable, or pleasing in the sight of another, especially God.
A city ruled by Shemeber whose king joined the battle in the vale of Siddim with the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Bela.
ZIPHITES, plural noun. The inhabitants of Ziph who twice informed Saul of David's hiding place near Hachilah and Jeshimon.
A Syrian kingdom or region whose soldiers were hired by the children of Ammon to fight against David. See ZOBAH.
